title: Root-Zone Media, Aeration, Water Holding and Buffering
summary: The root zone is a physical, chemical and biological environment whose air-filled porosity, water retention, density, buffering and irrigation history jointly shape root function.

sections.title: Air and water share pore space
sections.body: Container media must hold enough water to supply the plant while retaining pore space for gas exchange. Excess water saturation can reduce root-zone oxygen, while an overly coarse or poorly wetted medium can create rapid depletion and uneven root access to water.

sections.title: Media properties change irrigation behavior
sections.body: Particle size, composition, compaction, container geometry and root occupancy affect how water is retained and distributed. A watering schedule that works in one medium therefore should not be transferred automatically to a different substrate or container system.

sections.title: Chemical buffering affects nutrient behavior
sections.body: Cation exchange and substrate chemistry influence how ions are retained and exchanged near roots. Inert hydroponic substrates and chemically active organic/mineral media therefore require different expectations for pH, nutrient storage and response to irrigation inputs.
